.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Cool and dry weather continues through the weekend,
although a slow-moving Nor'easter off the coast will bring gusty
winds along the Chesapeake Bay and minor tidal flooding at times
through Friday.

Surface high pressure remains over the forecast area through  
the forecast period as a Nor'easter continues to drift offshore.
A tight pressure gradient between surface high pressure nearby
and the offshore Nor'easter yield gusty conditions daily, mainly
along and east of the I-95 corridor. Under high pressure,
temperatures moderate through Thursday with high temperatures 
in the 50s and 60s. Overnight low temperatures will be in the 
30s and 40s through Thursday night. Aloft, upper level troughing
develops across the eastern CONUS as ridging develops over 
central CONUS. By Thursday, the Nor'easter is absorbed into the 
upper trough and tracks off the coast of Maine. 

Surface high pressure builds southward out of southeastern
Canada and eastern Great Lakes regions into the mid-Atlantic
Friday through Monday. Dry conditions are expected each day,
while temperatures will be 5 to 10 degrees below average.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
VFR conditions continue as surface high pressure builds overhead
and dry conditions persist. Winds remain primarily out of the
north each day with terminals near the airport gusting around 15
knots in the afternoon. Otherwise, terminals can expect light
northerly winds, no precipitation, and VFR conditions. 

VFR conditions Friday through Saturday night. Winds generally north 
5 to 15 knots.

&&

.MARINE...
The Nor'easter off the Mid-Atlantic coast will deliver a 
prolonged period of SCA conditions (mainly over the 
central/lower waters). Small Craft Advisories remain in effect
through tonight and will likely need to be extended. The threat
is highest in the lower portions of the waters, with additional
Advisories possible through the end of the week. Otherwise, dry
conditions and non-hazardous marine weather is expected. 

Northerly flow with building high pressure could allow for Small 
Craft Advisories through midday Friday, then winds diminish and no 
marine hazards expected thereafter.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies will rise again through midweek as a Nor'easter
starts drifting northward offshore. Tidal locations including 
Dahlgren, Annapolis, Solomons Island, and Alexandria are 
forecast to reach minor flood stage by Tuesday night or 
Wednesday high tide cycles. Annapolis could approach moderate 
flood stage. However, some uncertainty remains on how exactly 
this Nor'easter will affect the tide levels. Elevated water 
levels likely won't decline until late in the week when the low 
will finally start pulling out to sea.

&&
